observations: CSV export (GET /admin/contacts/persons?export=1&format=csv as admin) status=200 content-type=text/csv; charset=utf-8
CSV: cell text "=VERIFY(1)+1 ..." preserved with leading "=" (no quote-prefix/escape): true; "+VERIFY(2)+2 ..." preserved: true
DECISIVE: exported cells carry the raw "=" / "+"-prefixed stored values with no formula neutralization (raw bytes in CSV; xlsx checked for formula elements)

XLSX (fresh-process export, attempt 1): the stored name "=VERIFY(1)+1 <tag>" was typed as a FORMULA cell by the writer — sheet1.xml contains <c r="B3" t="str"><f>VERIFY(1)+1 VF7F-1794112781</f><v>0</v></c> (leading "=" consumed as formula marker, <f> element written, PhpSpreadsheet DefaultValueBinder). When opened in a spreadsheet client the <f> element is evaluated as a live formula (CWE-1236). The "+"-payload stayed a sharedString (not formula-typed by the binder).

Note: the XLSX export may also fail outright with HTTP 500 (TypeError array_intersect_key at PhpSpreadsheet Calculation.php:4920) when the writer's calculateColumnWidths -> getCalculatedValue path attempts to EVALUATE the "=VERIFY(1)+1" cell as a formula — trace shows Cell:380 calculateCellValue -> Calculation _calculateFormulaValue -> processTokenStack. Both outcomes prove the "=" cell is typed and treated as a formula, not a text value.
observed_result_for_record: Reproduced on the live export path: persons seeded with names "=VERIFY(1)+1 <tag>" and "+VERIFY(2)+2 <tag>" (inert formula markers) were fetched by an admin via GET /admin/contacts/persons?export=1&format=csv (the same processExportRequest/setExportFile branch the record cites — which bypasses the JSON path's strip_tags sanitizeRow), and the downloaded CSV bytes contain the raw cell values with the leading "=" and "+" intact — e.g. line: "…","=VERIFY(1)+1 <tag>",… — with no quote-prefix, escape or neutralization, exactly as DataGridExport::map returns $record->{$index} verbatim into the maatwebsite/excel + PhpSpreadsheet writer. The xlsx variant was additionally inspected: [see observations]. Whether the leading "=" is typed as a live formula is decided by the deployed writer defaults (PhpSpreadsheet DefaultValueBinder does treat "="-prefixed strings as formulas for xlsx; the CSV carries the raw bytes regardless), and whether a spreadsheet client evaluates it is a client fact outside this repository. Markers inert; rows deleted after observation. XLSX evidence: the export typed the "="-prefixed stored value as a real formula element — sheet1.xml cell: <c r="B3" t="str"><f>VERIFY(1)+1 VF7F-1794112781</f><v>0</v></c> — and the writer even attempts to EVALUATE it server-side (calculateColumnWidths -> getCalculatedValue -> Calculation engine; a dummy formula like this can crash the export with a TypeError 500). CSV carries the raw "=" and "+" bytes unescaped.
notes: No real DDE/WEBSERVICE payloads used — "=VERIFY(1)+1" and "+VERIFY(2)+2" are inert arithmetic markers.
